text: UNION INSURANCE.

label: paragraph_title
text: Cunton Revival

label: text
text: With regard to what has been said about our long-standing friendly intercourse with the Cantonese, we doubtless all regret the present misunderstandings that have risen between us and look forward to a revival of the friendship and a renewal of business.

label: text
text: In these days it is no use/hiding one's light under a bushel, and the policy of expressing the Society's business in fine substantial buildings such as have been opened at Singapore and Sydney is, I venture to say, one of the best forms of propaganda and advertisement which can be made use of.

label: text
text: I feel confident that we can look forward to a continued increase in the results of the working of the Society, and I heartily endorse everything that has been said by the Chairman with reference to the ability and discrimination of the General Manager and staff in conducting the business.

label: text
text: I have much pleasure in second-ing the Report and Accounts.

label: paragraph_title
text: MR. ALVES' SPEECH.

label: text
text: Mr. Chairman,—I have listened to your speech with great interest and generally wish to support the statements made by Mr. Young in the second-in-the-adoption of the report and accounts. I am in agreement with most of his remarks, but I desire to emphasize one particular point which has not been sufficiently stressed upon, and that is the prosperity of the Society is, in my opinion, solely the result of one guiding hand.

label: text
text: In the nature of things, undertakings large or small rise or fall by the efforts of one person, and unorthodox as it may seem to you, it is my firm belief that the larger the undertaking the greater its probability of success, where its destinies and broad questions of policy are confined to the hands of a capable single person; and in this the Union, Insurance Society of Canton, has been fortunate in the past, and if I may say so, in the present; and I hope even to a greater degree in the future, if the accounts now before you are any criterion. As a large single shareholder, and representative of a still larger shareholder closely related to me, I feel that our interests are very ably looked after by the present General Manager in the person of Mr. Paul Lauden.

label: text
text: Whilst commending the policy of distributing only the income from investments which, I notice, as regards the working for the year 1924 was exceeded to the extent of some £20,000, I would urge the view that when the result of the working for 1925 is better known at this time next year, the distribution to shareholders might be enlarged moderately a little further, say to the extent of a further bonus of 5% per share, which would cost about £34,000 extra.

label: text
text: In connection with the dividends, there is a point in the accounts which no doubt is readily explainable. If you will refer to the working account for 1924 you will find the cost of the interim dividend at the rate of 24/- at £161.994; for 1925 the cost is given in the report at £162,000 which is certainly the correct figure. I have not the Balance Sheet at December 31, 1924 before me from which to ascertain the change in the issued capital which, no doubt, took place.

label: paragraph_title
text: "Shareholder TN Dark"

label: text
text: Without wishing to criticise the proposed adjustments as between the Reserve Fund and the Re-Insurance Fund, but only for enlightenment, I would ask the reason why the proposed transfer is limited only to £78,000. May I suggest that the transfer be increased to £178,000 raising the sterling Reserve Fund to £400,000. The Re-Insurance Fund will then stand at about 221/2 lakhs of pounds which should be ample capital to finance risks against that Fund. This appears to me all the stronger when viewed from the standpoint, that in whatever manner risks may be regarded or allocated by the management, the insurer will look to all the assets of the Society in satisfaction of claims. The fund is apparently of a finctuating nature, and whether or not it covers profits, the shareholders are now in the dark.

label: text
text:
Another fund of a fluctuating nature which moves more or less mysteriously unless analysed and compared with previous balance sheets is the Underwriting Suspense Account to which balances of Working Accounts are transferred after the lapse of a complete year, as with the case of the accounts for 1924 being considered to-day. Presumably claims, arising out of the working for 1924 and prior years, will be debited to this account, and I would like some information as to the amount debited during 1925 to the Underwriting Suspense Account for claims appertaining to 1928 and the years before that.
HOUSEHOLDERS' SUPPLIES

label: text
text: SERIOUS SITUATION

label: text
text: (Reuter's Service.)

label: text
text: London, May 27.

label: text
text: The seriousness of the coal situation is emphasised by an announcement by the Secretary of State for Mines that householders will only be allowed a half cwt. of coal weekly from to-morrow. They must fetch it themselves, and they must have a written permit from the local authorities. This is a quarter of the amount allowed in the smallest houses in war time. It is one of many restrictions imposed owing to dwindling supplies.

label: text
text: Business premises are cut down to half their usual supplies. No illuminated signs are allowed, and street lighting is reduced to a safety minimum.

label: text
text: A Whitehall communique published under the Emergency Powers Act in this connection adds that heavy penalties are provided for non-compliance with the above orders.

label: text
text:
The "Federation" of Master Printers and the Newspaper Society to-day agreed to a national settlement with the Printing and Kindred Trades, Federation providing for a continuance of the agreements existing prior to May 1.
It contains provisions for the prevention of lightning strikes, and stipulates that there shall be no interference with the contents of newspapers and periodicals published by members of the employers' organisations.

label: paragraph_title
text: Auditors' Position.

label: text
text: I would suggest that, in future years, this information be given in the face of the balance sheet, to enable shareholders to fully appreciate our "fortunes" after every working account is closed.

label: text
text: Another point to my mind of great importance is the question of auditors, one of whom is connected as a director of a company strenuously competing with this company. I refer to Messrs: Linstead and Davis, whose head, Mr. Bernard Brown, is a director of the Hongkong Fire Insurance Co., Ltd. Now, Gentlemen, I have nothing against Mr. Brown, but it is surely not good policy that our affairs should be intimately exposed to one of our auditors who is also actively in opposition to this company. The knowledge gained by Mr. Brown as an auditor may quite conceivably be superior to the knowledge of the directors themselves, and it is undesirable that he should have this knowledge in view of his directorship in the Hongkong Fire Insurance Co., although I feel certain that no information obtained as auditor is made use of.

label: text
text: I do not propose to vote against Messrs. Linstead and Davis re-election to-day, but will limit myself to the above opinion in the certainty that the matter will be duly taken up by the Board.

THE ANNUAL MEETING.

label: text
text: The annual meeting of the China Fire Insurance Co., Ltd., was held to-day at Union Building, it being stated that the company was in "such a strong position."

label: text
text: Mr. J. A. Plummer presided, supported by the Hon. Mr. A. O. Lang, Mr. T. G. Weall and Mr. W. L. Pattenden (directors) and Mr. Paul Lauder (general manager).

label: paragraph_title
text: Chairman's Review.

label: text
text: The chairman's address, after the usual reference to accounts, etc., was:

label: text
text: Gentlemen,—The working account for the year 1924 shows a balance of $715,063.75 to be dealt with. Your directors recommend that this balance be appropriated as follows:—

label: text
text: Dividend of $9 and bonus of $5 per share on 20,000 shares, $280,000.00.

label: text
text: To be carried forward to underwriting suspense account, $435,063.75.

label: text
text: The balance at credit of the 1925 account is $904,610,30.

label: text
text: It gives your directors much pleasure to be able to present to you an annual report showing the Company to be in such a strong position.

label: text
text: You will notice from the working accounts that the actual nett premium shows a decrease in comparison with last year. This was anticipated, however, and represents the consequence of the curtailment of business, the results of which did not in the opinion of our management justify the liability incurred.

label: text
text: It is anticipated that the balance of 1925 working account will shown a satisfactory result.

label: text
text: I may mention that the figures throughout—the accounts are affected by exchange. The sterling rate taken at December 31, 1925 being 2/4.3/8 as against a corresponding rate at December 31, 1924 of 2/3.3/4. This, of course, means a drop in the dollar equivalent of all sterling so far as this year's accounts are concerned.

label: text
text: As I have already stated, the balance sheet shows a very strong position and you will notice, Gentlemen, the total assets are now over $8,450,000.

label: text
text: The reinsurance fund and underwriting "suspense accounts show a satisfactory increase."

label: text
text: I am sure you will have noted with pleasure that the dividend and bonus this year have been increased by the sum of $2 each.

label: text
text: I now move that the directors' report and statement as presented be adopted and when this has been seconded, I shall be pleased to answer any question that may be put.

label: text
text: Mr. G. S. Archbutt seconded. No question was put and the motion was carried unanimously.

label: text
text: 'Other business passed by the meeting comprised:—

label: text
text: Re-election of Mr. J. A. Plummer and Mr. T. G. Weall as directors — proposed by Mr. A. Sommerfelt, seconded by Mr. V. R. V. Ribeiro.

label: text
text: Re-election of Messrs. Lowe, Bingham and Matthews and Messrs. Linstead and Davis, as auditors for the current year, at $750 each—proposed by Mr. A. A. Alves, seconded by Mr. F. H. Farne.

In addition to missing his boat (the s.s. "Elkridge"), on which he claimed to be employed, S. Anderson appeared at the police station this morning with wet clothing and cuts over his eyes.
His complaint was that a number of men attacked him at 5 a.m. and, that not being enough, they threw him into the harbour. He added that he got ashore with the greatest difficulty.

label: paragraph_title
text: AFTER FIVE YEARS.

label: text
text: COMMENTS ON DOWNFALL

label: paragraph_title
text: (Reuter's Service.)

label: text
text:
Abd el Krim's surrender does not merely end the career of the world's most picturesque figure, whose five years guerrilla warfare against two European Powers began by a crushing defeat of the Spaniards in 1921, but probably terminates the secular quarrel between the Moors and Spaniards.
Abd el Krim, no ignorant mountaineer, was the guest of the Government of Madrid, for two years before he attacked them. As a result of his special course of study in Madrid, he engaged foreigners to teach the tribesmen methods of modern warfare, and he controlled the Riffan troops by means of an extensive telephone system.

label: text
text: Among the political consequences of the Riffan adventure has been the establishment of a Dictatorship in Spain, and the recognition by France of the necessity of close Franco-Spanish co-operation in Morocco, while the downfall of Abd el Krim will have repercussions in the whole of the Moslem world.

label: text
text: The “Times,” in an editorial, hopes Abd el Krim's correspondence will be published in order to reveal to the world the intrigues of the mining concessionales and financiers who exploited Riff cupidity and fanaticism.

label: paragraph_title
text: Surrender Expected

label: paragraph_title
text: Tanglers, May 27.

label: text
text: The surrender of Abd el Krim was not surprising, as it was known he was in flight, if not hiding, fearing assassination by his disappointed followers. The French had captured the greater part of Jebel Hamman, the mountain fastness which was Abd el Krim's last sanctuary.

label: text
text: His own tribe, the Beni Wariaghel, had submitted, and practically the whole Riff territory was in the hands of the French and Spanish.

label: text
text: The only two trilies intact, the Ghomara and Djebela, were apparently unaware of Abd el Krim's collapse.

label: text
text: End Welcomed.

label: text
text: France's great sigh of relief at the surrender of Abd-el-Krim rustles the pages of the newspapers which joyfully welcome the end of the Riff "venture, which, they emphasise, there must be no repetition. The Riff must henceforth be properly governed," in connection with which the continuance of Franco-Spanish co-operation "is underlined in order to exploit the wealth of Morocco.

label: text
text: It is suggested that Abd-el-Krim will not be permitted to reside in Moslem territory and may be compelled to apologise to the Sultan of Morocco.

label: paragraph_title
text: Bolshevist Dreams.

label: text
text: Le Matin describes Abd-el-Krim's surrender as the dissipation of a German and Bolshevik dream of France's ruin in Morocco. It adds: "For all her 1,700,000 dead France has shown once again that she can defend herself. Abd-el-Krim can rely on our clemency, but a pardon does not signify forgetfulness. We shall remember his dealings with the Bolsheviks and Pangermans."

label: paragraph_title
text: Good For Briand.

label: text
text: Tantamount to a vote of confidence, the Chamber of Deputies by 320 votes in 209 agreed to the Government's demand for an adjournment of interpellations on the financial situation.

label: text
text: Undoubtedly the recovery of the franc, followed by the collapse of Abd-el-Krim, has greatly strengthened M. Briand's position.

label: paragraph_title
text: WORLD'S COMMERCE.

label: text
text: His Majesty the King granted an audience to the forty delegates of the International Parliamentary Commercial Conference. His Majesty recalling the 1918 Conference, when only eight countries were represented, thought the present encouraging increase indicated a general desire to assist reparation, and the injuries the War inflicted on the world's commerce.

label: text
text: His Majesty picked out from the Conference's agenda the production and distribution of coal, shipping law and Customs which he declared was of vital importance to Britain and doubtless to other countries.

label: text

label: text
text: MEETING TO CONFIRM.

label: text

label: text
text: New York, May 27,

label: text
text: The International Mercantile Marine Company will hold a meeting on June 17 to confirm the proposed sale of the Oceanic Steam Navigation Company, otherwise known as the White Star Line, to British interests headed by Furness, Withy and Company for about £7,500,000. It is understood in connection with the sale that the vendors agree to limit competition in the present White Star trade routes.

label: paragraph_title
text: PREVIOUS NEWS.

label: text
text: The following cables on the subject were published a month ago:

label: text
text: A sensation has been caused in shipping circles at Liverpool by the reported offer of British interests to purchase the White Star line, in which connection Baron Kylsant's name is prominently mentioned.

label: paragraph_title
text: "Wall Street's View"

label: paragraph_title
text: New York, April 24.

label: text
text: Mr. J. P. Morgan and Mr. Charles Steels, members of J. P. Morgan and Company, have both resigned their directorships of the International Mercantile Marine Corporation and their action is interpreted in Wall Street as intimating that the negotiations for the purchase of the White Star line have practically been completed.

label: text
text: It is recalled that the late J. Pierpont Morgan founded this corporation, which owns the controlling interest in the White Star line.

label: text
text:
The J. P. Morgan Company have issued a statement saying that the resignations of Mr. J. P. Morgan and Charles Steels were prompted by the fact that their London partner might be interested in the contemplated sale of some of the properties of the International Mercantile Marine Corporation.
It is reported that both the Cunard Steamship Company and Furness, Withy and Co., Ltd., have made bids for the White Star fleet, and there is a prospect of the transference of the line to the Cunard Steamship Company for a price of about $35,000,000.

label: text

label: text
text: In reply to an enquiry with regard to the offer of the purchase of the White Star line Baron Klyssant stated that he knew nothing at all about it.

New York, April 23.
A cash offer for the White Star Line received from certain British interests will be considered at a special meeting of the Directors of the International Mercantile Marine Corporation today.

London, May 27
A Chinese seaman employed on the sea. “Fembrokeshire” charged at East Ham, with concealing 63 automatic pistols, two walking sticks, guns, and 6,700 rounds of ammunition, told the Customs that the arms were given to him at Antwerp by a Cantonese, who asked him to take them to Hongkong, promising him $3 for each gun delivered.
The seaman was fined $156 or three months' imprisonment with labour.
The body of a woman found floating in the harbour near the Wing Lok Street wharf yesterday was brought ashore by two Chinese firemen. Artificial respiration brought the woman round and she was sent to hospital.
